claims.text: High-throughput computational modeling incorporating first-principles and thermophysical-parameter calculations can overcome current limitations in characterizing high-entropy alloys.
The proposed intervention can accurately determine melting temperature.
The proposed intervention can accurately determine enthalpy and entropy of fusion.
The proposed intervention can accurately determine volume change upon melting.
The proposed intervention can accurately determine liquid thermodynamic properties.
The proposed intervention is efficient across a large compositional space.
The intervention consists of high-throughput computational modeling that combines first-principles calculations with thermophysical-parameter calculations.
The proposed modeling approach applies to high-temperature solid states of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The proposed modeling approach applies to liquid states of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Phase stability acts as a structural mediator between the computational intervention and the predicted properties.
Morphology acts as a structural mediator between the computational intervention and the predicted properties.
High-throughput computational models can efficiently predict phase stability.
High-throughput computational models can efficiently predict the targeted melting and liquid thermodynamic properties.
The intervention will improve accuracy relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve property availability and determination efficiency relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The hypothesis is limited to high-entropy alloys under high-temperature conditions.
The accuracy of high-throughput models for predicting phase stability and thermodynamic properties is uncertain.
Failure to predict experimental properties within a specified error margin would falsify the hypothesis.
